digest.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 brings a near-frontier small model at $0.10 per million input tokens, OpenAI publishes 722 math manuscripts, and Common Sense calls ChatGPT for Teens an 'Unacceptable Risk'
digest.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7. It's the first Haiku with effort settings and adaptive thinking, has a 1M-token context, and costs $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens up to 100K-token prompts. Artificial Analysis scores it 43 on its Intelligence Index, 26 points above the last Haiku and just behind Kimi K3, but at max effort it uses about 162K output tokens per task, roughly 3x GPT-6 Luna. Alongside it, Anthropic halved Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices and added monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers. OpenAI released 722 math manuscripts from an unreleased internal model, grouped into 372 result families with Lean proofs for 162 of them. Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute rated ChatGPT for Teens an 'Unacceptable Risk' after 4,000+ test prompts; OpenAI disputes the testing. Tooling: Codex 0.161.0 makes GPT-6.1 Sol the default and adds `/mcp login`, Pi 1.1.0 adds Haiku 5.5 and `+name/-name` tool tweaks, and Claude Code 2.1.293–2.1.294 adds Haiku 5.5 and fixes prompt hooks.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5: 1M context at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens
stories.dek: Released October 7, Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku with adjustable effort (Low through Max) and adaptive thinking. It costs $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens for prompts up to 100K tokens and $0.50/$2.50 above that; Anthropic estimates real workloads cost about 75% less than on Haiku 4.5. Anthropic reports 1620 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1 (Haiku 4.5: 735), 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1, 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and 57.4% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools. It's available as `claude-haiku-5-5` on the Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Anthropic also halved Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices and added monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers.
stories.whyItMatters: Anthropic is pitching it for subagents, compaction, classification, and browser automation, the high-volume parts of agent workloads where model cost adds up fastest.

stories.title: Artificial Analysis scores Haiku 5.5 at 43, but it uses far more tokens than GPT-6 Luna
stories.dek: Haiku 5.5 at max effort scores 43 on the AA Intelligence Index, ahead of GLM-5.3 Flash (42) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (41), just behind Kimi K3 (44), and 13 points below Sonnet 5.5. The catch is token use: about 162K output tokens per Intelligence Index task at max, more than Opus 5.5 at max and roughly 3x GPT-6 Luna. At high effort it needs about 55K tokens to reach scores similar to Luna's (about 50K). AA also measured 33% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 1578 Elo on AA-Briefcase.
stories.whyItMatters: The low per-token price doesn't tell you the whole cost. Run Haiku 5.5 at high or medium effort unless you need max, or you'll pay for tokens you don't need.

stories.title: OpenAI releases 722 math manuscripts from an unreleased internal model
stories.dek: On October 6 OpenAI published 722 manuscripts, grouped into 372 result families across 17 fields, in an Apache 2.0 GitHub repository along with abridged summaries of the model's reasoning. The model was given about 4,000 problems, and each accepted result cost about three hours of ChatGPT Pro reasoning on average. Lean formalizations cover the main result of 162 of the papers. The model itself remains closed.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the largest batch of AI-generated math so far, and Lean proofs back less than a quarter of it. Checking the rest falls to human mathematicians.

stories.title: Common Sense Media rates ChatGPT for Teens an 'Unacceptable Risk'
stories.dek: The Youth AI Safety Institute tested more than 4,000 prompts on accounts registered to 13- to 17-year-olds. It found that teens could discuss self-harm for long stretches without parents on newly linked accounts being notified, and that ChatGPT missed more than one in four warranted crisis referrals. Study mode was easy to bypass, and adult-registered accounts never switched to the under-18 experience even when the user said they were 13. The group wants independent verification before OpenAI resumes marketing to teens. OpenAI says the tests don't reflect how its safeguards work.
stories.whyItMatters: 'Unacceptable Risk' is the top of the Institute's five-level scale. Coming days after the New York City Council hearing, it adds pressure for binding rules on teen safety.

stories.title: Mistral Large 4 scores 38 on the AA index, the best model from outside the US and China
stories.dek: Mistral released Large 4 in Research Public Preview on October 6. It's a 1T-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters, and Mistral plans to release the weights at the end of October. Artificial Analysis scores it 38 on its Intelligence Index, level with GPT-6 Luna and just below DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. That's a big jump from Mistral Large 3 (9) and Mistral Medium 3.5 (14). Artificial Analysis lists pricing at $1.36/$4.18 per million tokens, halved for the first two weeks.
stories.whyItMatters: Europe now has an open-weight model close to the frontier. It's still 20 points behind Opus 5.5, though, and seven Chinese open models still rank above it.

stories.title: Meta and Sierra publish the Personal Agent Protocol, a sign-in standard for AI agents
stories.dek: Announced October 6, PAP builds on OAuth so a personal agent can show a business who it is, which user it represents, and what that user authorized: read-only or write, with sessions that carry across web, API, and chat. A v0.1 spec is due later in October. Walmart, Shopify, Stripe, Genesys, and Instinct are partners; OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon are not. It comes after Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent on September 20. Bret Taylor said it's 'kind of chaos until such a standard exists.'
stories.whyItMatters: Agent commerce now has several competing identity standards (Visa, Google, OpenAI, and now PAP), and the big retailers are backing more than one of them.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores. October 7: added Mistral Large 4 (AA 38, research preview Oct 6); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Reflection's Beam is not listed because it has only self-reported scores. October 8: added Claude Haiku 5.5 (AA 43 at max effort, released Oct 7); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet.

harness.notes: 2.1.294 fixes `prompt` and `agent` hooks that were written as instructions allowing actions they should have blocked, and judges `prompt` hooks on Stop and SubagentStop better so sessions stop early less often. 2.1.293 (Oct 7) adds Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`, 1M context), `agentType` in the `subagentStatusLine` payload so you can tell custom subagent types apart, and `isDeferred` on `$.tool.register` so mods can keep a tool's schema behind tool search. It also fixes compaction memory leaks and many Remote Control, cloud session, plugin, and Slack bugs. 2.1.292 (Oct 6) added per-subagent `effort`.

GPT-6.1 Sol is now the default model in the bundled and Amazon Bedrock catalogs, and Bedrock gets multi-agent V2 and Ultra reasoning. New `/mcp login <name>` signs in to an MCP server without leaving the TUI. Daybreak cyber routing is now strictly opt-in (`--enable cli_daybreak`), and `codex exec --cyber-access-program` picks a Cyber access program per turn. Fixes: approved filesystem escalation keeps denied reads and network limits, launch permissions survive reconnects, SQLite corruption is caught earlier and backed up, and retries follow server retry guidance under overload. 0.162.0 alphas continue.

Adds Claude Haiku 5.5 (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`, adaptive thinking up to xhigh/max). `--tools` now takes `+name`/`-name` entries (for example `pi -t +codemode,-write`) that adjust the default tool set instead of replacing it. Pi reports program status over OSC 7501, so supporting terminals and dashboards can show whether it's working, blocked, done, or failed. GPT-6 Luna and native llama.cpp decision models work as classifiers, and codemode's `models.classify()` accepts images. Fixes: standalone binaries no longer load `.env` files from the launch directory, and `pi update` prunes old releases.

extensions.name: LMCP
extensions.blurb: A free Mac app that turns the apps you already use (Mail, Calendar, Teams, Slack, WhatsApp, iMessage, Outlook, OneDrive, Google Drive, Zoom, Office files, the browser, and the terminal) into 190+ MCP tools for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other clients. It reads local caches where it can, so most apps need no API keys or OAuth setup. The installer configures supported clients automatically.

extensions.name: AWS MCP Server (six new regions)
extensions.blurb: AWS's managed MCP server, which gives coding agents one interface to AWS APIs, is now available in Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Ireland, London, and Oregon. Teams outside us-east can keep agent traffic in their own region.

extensions.name: Trustgrid MCP Server
extensions.blurb: The October 6 update lets agents run interactive, websocket-backed node tools such as `ping` and `arping` through Trustgrid's MCP server, which turns an agent into a hands-on network diagnostics assistant for edge nodes.

tips.title: Use Haiku 5.5 for subagents, at high effort rather than max
tips.body: Haiku 5.5 is built for subagent and compaction work and costs a fraction of Sonnet. Artificial Analysis found that at max effort it burns about 162K output tokens per task, about 3x GPT-6 Luna, while at high effort it lands near Luna's scores on about 55K. Combine it with Claude Code's per-subagent `effort` parameter: send search and summary subagents to Haiku at medium or high effort.

tips.title: Tweak the default tool set instead of restating it
tips.body: Pi 1.1.0 accepts `+name` and `-name` in `--tools`, so `pi -t +codemode,-write` keeps the default tools, adds codemode, and drops write. That's handy for a read-only review run without listing every tool. It combines with the `mcp__server__*` globs from 1.0.4.

tips.title: Re-auth MCP servers mid-session with /mcp login
tips.body: When an MCP server's token expires partway through a Codex session, you no longer need to quit. Codex 0.161.0's `/mcp login <name>` runs the sign-in from the active TUI, and the session keeps its context. Enterprise MCP sign-in now also fails closed when the config refresh fails.
